Inputs: this is a delta review over the first record (the PASS on `f4345a9d68b9693e5e2b790f3e15234ff344ca93`, 2026-10-30, claim 6525641438); the delta `git diff f4345a9d6..1a9e3f73a` (1 file, +6 / −3 within the one blockquote note, two commits `ea406edf` and `1a9e3f73`, author `Claude`, trailers `Co-authored-by` and `Claude-Session` present, no model name, no `Refs`); the whole `git diff 27e0bd584..1a9e3f73a` (1 file, +28 / −1); `git merge-base pr-28161 origin/main` is `27e0bd584`; `origin/main` had moved eight commits to `9f13ee815` at review time (the four the first record saw, then #28136, #28141, #28132, #28151) and none of them touches the ADR, any cited file, `scripts/pm`, or the two gates; the PR body (unchanged since the first head) and its two comments (6525641438, the claim on the first head; 6526256844, the claim naming this session and this head, 2026-10-30T15:17Z; no reviews, no hold, no hand-off); card #28038 (body, triage 6521083653, claim 6525245002; no comment since the first record); #27992 / PR #28014, #27237, #28016 / PR #28037 as the first record read them; the dispatch order and the dev report at /mnt/project-files/skills-lane-seat2/; .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md and review-checklist.md; AGENTS.md Prime Directive #13; the full ADR-0097 at this head and at the base; the code at `origin/main` for every symbol the note cites and for every path the three new claims rest on; the head's check-runs (three polls, last at 2026-10-30T15:21Z, all completed); micromark 4.0.2 and marked 16.4.2 (a sibling checkout's copies) for the rendering reading.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set: unchanged — correct.** The diff against the base is ADR prose only: one blockquote note of 26 lines inserted after the third degraded-section bullet (:199-224 at this head), and one entry appended to the `Amended by` header line (the −1 is that line rewritten with the entry added; every prior entry is byte-identical). The delta since the first head rewrites three sentences inside the note and adds one; it adds no anchor, touches no other line, and moves nothing in any schema, export, type or runtime path. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold.
2. **Which degraded instances are held — the note's two cases are exactly the code's two (carried over, re-read on `origin/main`, unchanged lines).** `held: true` is written at two sites of `plugin.ts` and nowhere else: `failDegradedConnectorInstance` (:2580), reached from the factory catch when the thrown value is neither a credential rejection nor `CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`, the run is soft and the name is already in `degradedInstances` (:2383-2384); and `holdConnectorForRejectedCredential` (:3105), where `held = info.credential === undefined || stored !== undefined` (:3102) — a credential written into the declaration, or a value whose `source` is `object` (the `sys_connector_credential` row). An environment or vault value takes the else branch (:3106-3114): attempts counted, no `held`, the refusal recorded in `credentialRefusals`. The note's held list is complete and true, and its backoff parenthetical names true members of the other set (`degradeConnectorInstance`, and the env/vault branch) without claiming to be exhaustive.
3. **Delta (a), the configuration-fault sentence — now the code's own definition (should-fix 1 of the first record, folded).** The note reads "a configuration fault met by an instance that is already degraded, on its backoff retry or on a `metadata:reloaded` reconcile". The guard is `!opts.fatal && this.degradedInstances.has(name)` (:2383); the comment above it says "its backoff retry, or a reload" (:2380-2381); the method's docblock says "neither the retry timer nor an unchanged reload re-attempts it" (:2562-2563). The two paths the note names are the two the code names: the retry timer runs `materializeDeclaredConnectors(ctx, { fatal: false })` (:3342) and the `metadata:reloaded` hook (:1666) runs the reload mode, `fatal: false` (:2036). Observation, no fix owed: the guard is on soft runs as a class, so the reconcile a credential write or clear runs (:2937, :2970) and the one a peer's credential signal runs (:2985-2988) would hold a configuration fault the same way; the ADR's own third bullet already names the soft reconcile by its hook (`metadata:reloaded`), and the note follows that spelling, so a reader of this file reads it as the soft-reconcile class. The header entry's "met on a retry" (:8) is a summary that the third bullet's own wording ("retried on an exponential backoff ... and immediately by any reconcile") covers.
4. **Not retried: both skips are as stated (carried over).** `scheduleDeclarativeRetry` (:3332) arms the timer over the `degradedInstances` values filtered to `!d.held` (:3336); `reconcileDeclaredConnectors` (:2221-2222) does `if (held?.held && held.signature === signature) continue;`. The note's "the backoff timer skips it ... and so does a reconcile while its signature is unchanged" is those two lines.
5. **Delta (b) and (c), the re-attempt sentences — true, and the new sentence is traced end to end.** "An edit of its declaration, setting its stored credential again (the row's revision is part of the signature), or a restart re-attempts it" drops the first head's "Only", which the next sentence would have contradicted. The three named ways stand as the first record read them: the per-instance signature is `connectorInstanceSignature(bound)` plus `|credential:` and `connectorCredentialFingerprint(...)` (:2171-2173), which returns `object:${row.revision}` for a stored row (`connector-credentials.ts` :537), so a `PUT` (`store.set` returns the new revision, :2925; then a soft reconcile, :2937) changes the signature and passes the held-skip; a declaration edit changes `connectorInstanceSignature`; a restart empties the in-memory map. The new sentence, "Clearing the stored credential also ends the hold, since the reference's fingerprint changes: the instance then degrades for the missing reference and goes back on the backoff", is each of four facts in the code: (i) the clear triggers a reconcile — `clearConnectorCredential` (:2949) calls `store.clear(ref, userId)` (:2959), which deletes the `sys_connector_credential` row (`connector-credentials.ts` :351-358, `engine.delete` at :357), then `reconcileDeclaredConnectors(ctx, { fatal: false })` (:2970) on the reconcile queue, as its docblock says (:2942-2947: "remove the stored value for one reference, then reconcile: every instance naming it is torn down and registered degraded, naming the reference"); (ii) the fingerprint changes — with the row gone `connectorCredentialFingerprint` falls through :537 to :539 and returns `vault` or `missing` instead of `object:N`, so the signature at :2173 differs from the held record's and the skip at :2222 no longer fires (the stale refusal record for the reference is also dropped, :2178-2181); (iii) what runs sets no held flag — with nothing answering the reference `resolveConnectorCredential` returns `{ kind: 'missing' }` (`connector-credentials.ts` :582), the reconcile routes to `degradeConnectorForCredential` (:2273-2277), and that method writes `{ attempts, signature, reason }` to `degradedInstances` with no `held` (:2731-2735) and registers the husk with no hold (:2740), the reason being `missingCredentialReason` (:2721-2722); (iv) a missing reference is on the backoff — the record has no `held`, so the `!d.held` filter at :3336 keeps it, and the method's docblock says so ("Both retry on the #3017 backoff", :2705). `connectors.mdx` :341-342 says the same for `DELETE`. One edge, consistent with the sentence's point and not owed a fix: when the host's resolver answers the reference after the clear, the fingerprint is `vault`, the hold ends the same way, and the reconcile re-attempts with that value instead of degrading for a missing one; a refusal of that value takes the env/vault branch (:3112-3113), which is on the backoff — never held.
6. **The husk carries the hold (carried over).** `registerDegradedConnector` (`plugin-extension-api.ts` :363-380) spreads `degradedHold: hold` into the `RegisteredConnector`; both hold sites pass it (`{ kind: 'declaration' }` at :2589, and `stored ? { kind: 'credential', ref: stored.ref } : { kind: 'declaration' }` at :3126); `getConnectorDegradedHold` (`engine.ts` :4189-4192) reads it back only while `state === 'degraded'`. A later unheld degrade of the same name (the cleared-credential path of ①.5, `registerDegradedConnector` at :2740 with no hold) replaces the record without `degradedHold`, which is what "goes back on the backoff" means for the dispatch refusal.
7. **The refusal wording is PR #28037's, verbatim (carried over).** `connector-nodes.ts` :75-84 and `describeHold` (`plugin-extension-api.ts` :401-403). The note's two quoted held strings and its one quoted backoff string are those, character for character (the second held string abbreviated with an ellipsis and a placeholder for the reference name, which is fair), and `connector-held-dispatch-refusal.test.ts` :106, :119, :135 pins them.
8. **Delta (d), the placeholder — now a code span, and it renders literally (should-fix 2 of the first record, folded).** At :221 the reference placeholder sits in a code span inside the plain quotes. Rendered with micromark 4.0.2 (CommonMark) and marked 16.4.2 (`gfm: true`), the new line yields a `code` element whose text is the escaped placeholder, so the page reads "until credential 'ref-placeholder' is set again" with the placeholder visible; the first head's bare spelling rendered as a raw HTML tag in marked (which GitHub's sanitizer drops, as the first record said). CommonMark §6.1 is the rule: HTML is not parsed inside a code span. The spelling now matches the corpus (ADR-0079 :141, ADR-0116 :50, ADR-0137 :63).
9. **Anchors: seven added at the first head, none since, all resolve, and the gate holds them.** Local probe on this head: 2850 anchors, 630 symbol (604 declaration, 26 literal), 2173 file-level, 47 cross-repo, exit 0 — the same figures as the first head and as the dev reports; base `27e0bd584` 2843 / 623 (597, 26) per the first record. The delta adds no anchor (`git diff` shows no new backticked path). The `Lint · docs & code guards` check-run, the job that runs `check:adr-symbol-anchors`, is success on this head.
10. **adr-index: no change owed.** `node scripts/adr-index.mjs` on this head prints "unchanged docs/adr/README.md (235 lines)" and the porcelain is empty; `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, the job that runs `check:adr-index`, is success on this head.
11. **Citations, numbers and dates (carried over, untouched by the delta).** #27992 / PR #28014 (merged 2026-10-30T08:38Z, `066ff51e2`), #27237 (closed 2026-10-29), #28016 / PR #28037 (merged 2026-10-30T10:36Z, `b59bf60c8`) — all ancestors of the base or closed before the amendment's date; the card's "not before PR #28037 merges" condition is met.
12. **PR body declarations (carried over; see ③ for the stale Verification head).** `Fixes #28038` on its own line; no closing keyword beside any other card number. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; the six `## 维护者速读` lines present. Labels `documentation`, `size/s`, `skip-changeset`; author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; draft; base `main`.
13. **Register.** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 28161` on this head: 1 of 1 path hits (`docs/adr/**`), GOVERNED, Tier H, 29 changed lines (+28 / −1) under the human-merge threshold.

### ② Semver level

No release. `skip-changeset` is right: the diff publishes nothing from any released package (one ADR file under `docs/adr/`, which no package's `files[]` ships); no changeset family is derived for a docs-only diff. On this head the `Check Changeset` check-run is skipped rather than success: the `synchronize` run's payload already carries the `skip-changeset` label, so the job's `if:` fast path (`pr-automation.yml` :308-309, the `skip-changeset` opt-out its comment at :266 names) skips it without a runner, where the first head's success came from the `labeled` event's run. Same verdict, cheaper path. `Clause-②: no` is right; no narrowing is declared or present.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags: no `open_questions`. The three declared deviations of the first record stand unchanged ((1) `skip-changeset` carried on `pr_create`, accepted; (2) `dispatch-gates --tier` reads `docs/adr/**` as a MANDATORY fable tier while the dev ran on opus/medium — this record is the compensating CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER review; (3) `pnpm lint` not run locally — `Lint · ESLint` is success on this head). The two fold commits carry the same trailers as the first.
- Independence: the delta was produced by `session_016WV4cypdG8XcEafFNG2EFa` on `claude/project-thread-8t7yh8` (the card thread's platform-assigned branch, the recorded exception the claim names); this record is rendered by `session_016WV4d1QkPVVzNz3FJqb2iS`, which did not draft it. Claim comment 6526256844 names this session and this head; no competing claim, hold or hand-off; no reviews on the PR.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no non-bot login to record.
- Tier: H by the register (`docs/adr/**`); the maintainer or a GOVERNED_APPROVERS review lands it. Draft PR; nothing to disarm.
- CI (41 check-runs on this head, all completed at the last poll, 2026-10-30T15:21Z): 25 success, 16 skipped by path or design, 0 failure, 0 in progress. Success includes both required jobs (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`) and their sub-jobs: `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (runs `check:adr-index`), `Lint · docs & code guards` (runs `check:adr-symbol-anchors`), `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, the three `Lint · scoped` jobs, `Type Check · workspace`, `· source gates`, `· consumer gates`, `· debt ledger`; plus `Test Core` and `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test UI`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Auto Label`, `filter`. Skipped: `Check Changeset` (the label opt-out, ②), the UI build, lint, type-check and test shards, Build Docs, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, UI Published Artifacts, the opt-in harnesses, the schedule gate, the UI `Live E2E`. The first head's 46 were the same set plus the `opened` and `labeled` event runs' duplicates. The all-green condition for landing is met on this head.
- PR body versus head: the body's Verification section still says "All readings at head `f4345a9d`", and its "What changes" bullets paraphrase the first head's wording (the "first met on a backoff retry" clause, the "only an edit ..." sentence, the bare placeholder). The relay cannot patch a PR body. This does not matter for landing: every number the body cites was re-measured on this head here and is identical (anchors 2850 / 630, `check:adr-index` unchanged, GOVERNED 1 of 1, 21 dispatch-gates families — `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` is success on this head); the only figure that moved is the line count, +25 to +28, which the body states nowhere as a number (the `size/s` label is live); and the governed text a maintainer approves is the diff, not the body's paraphrase of it. Recorded here so the stale head cite is read as stale and not as a claim about this head.
- Not re-run here: the dev's 21 dispatch-gates families (read from the report; `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` is success on this head); the service-automation test suite (the wording is read from the test file and from the source it exercises, not executed); the base reading of the anchor gate (the first record's, at the same base).

### ④ Design judgment

Rules face, `docs/adr/0097-declarative-connector-instances.md`, against its first consumer and its execution plan:

- **Prime Directive #13 and the ADR's own convention — hold.** The three degraded-section bullets (:186-197) are context lines in the diff, byte for byte; the note opens by saying the first and third "are kept as written; they now hold only for an instance on the backoff", so the recorded sentences stand and the amendment sits beside them. The form is this file's own: a blockquote paragraph opening with the bold `Amendment note (date, #card — provenance).` head, the spelling of all five prior notes in 0097, placed directly under the bullets it qualifies. The `Amended by` header entry follows the three existing entries' shape. The Status line is right to be unchanged: this ADR's Status has never carried an amendment, unlike ADR-0066; the convention is per file. The delta keeps all of this: it edits only the note's inside.
- **First consumer.** The reader deciding what a degraded instance's dispatch refusal means now reads a section that is true against `origin/main` as a definition and not only as an instance: the hold is anchored to the two sites that set it with the guard's own two paths, the two skips, the four ways out (edit, set again, clear, restart) with the mechanism for each, the husk's carrier and the two refusal spellings. The seven anchors bind the prose to the symbols: a rename or move of any of them turns `check:adr-symbol-anchors` red, which is what the card asked for.
- **Execution plan.** Nothing is left to implement: the mechanism (PR #28014, #27237) and the wording (PR #28037) are on `main` and the amendment records them after the fact. The clearing sentence adds no mechanism; it names one `connectors.mdx` :341-342 and `clearConnectorCredential`'s docblock already state.
- **No contradiction elsewhere (carried over, re-checked for the new sentence).** The first record's `git grep` over `skills/**`, `content/docs/**` and `docs/adr/**` stands (no sentence promises a retry for every degraded instance). The new clearing sentence agrees with `connectors.mdx` :341-342 ("`DELETE` removes the stored value. The instances naming the reference are torn down and registered degraded again") and with the 2026-10-28 §6 note's unresolved-`credentialRef`-on-the-backoff reading. The observation outside this PR stands: ADR-0143's revoked-grant "not retried into existence" is a third not-retried kind with no code on `main` today (should-fix 3).
- **Rendering.** Folded; ①.8.
- **The tier deviation.** The diff is 28 lines of prose; this review read every cited symbol, the two routing sites around them, the clear and set paths end to end, the test that pins the wording, and the two docs surfaces that restate the rule, all at `origin/main`. Nothing in the diff is under-reviewed because of the model the dev ran on.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：ADR-0097 的 degraded 一节后面加一段带日期的修订注（2026-10-30），原有三条要点一字不改，头部加一条 Amended-by。注里说清楚这几件事：
  - 有两类 degraded 实例是「held」的，不会被 backoff 重试：
    - 已经 degraded 的实例，在 backoff 重试或 `metadata:reloaded` 重新协调时遇到配置错误（#27992）；
    - 上游拒绝了凭据，而这个凭据存在 `sys_connector_credential` 或直接写在声明里（#27237）。
  - 能解除 held 的只有四种操作：改声明、重新设置存储的凭据、清掉存储的凭据（清掉后改为因缺引用而 degraded，回到 backoff）、重启。
  - 派发到 held 实例时，报错会写明怎么解除（#28016 / PR #28037）。
  - 「平台会自动重试」这句话只对 backoff 上的实例成立。

  只改了 1 个文件，+28/−1。
- 为什么改：PR #28014 和 #28037 合并后，ADR 原文「degraded 实例会自动重试」对 held 实例已经不成立。
- 风险与回滚：只改文本。新增 7 个符号锚点，全部能解析（623 → 630），`adr-index` 没有变化。回滚就是 revert。
- 先看：ADR-0097 第 199 行起的 Amendment note。
- 两分钟验证：`node scripts/check-adr-symbol-anchors.mjs` exit 0。
- 需要你做的：登记册判为 Tier H（`docs/adr/**`），**需要 os-zhuang 或 hotlong 批准**。契约复核 PASS，记录就在本评论前面，`Head-sha: 1a9e3f73a2bdc9ea3f196a907e9a37d317d91bda`。批准后由批准人或本席转 ready、入队。

席位意见：ACCEPT。契约复核分两轮：
- 首轮在 `f4345a9d` 上 PASS，提了两条 should-fix：重载时也会 held；尖括号占位符在 GitHub 上渲染成空。
- 本席没有直接贴首轮记录，而是让卡线程先把这两条修进同一段注，再做增量复核（`1a9e3f73`），结果 PASS，没有 must-fix。
- 复核逐句对过代码：held 只在 `failDegradedConnectorInstance` 和 `holdConnectorForRejectedCredential` 两处设置；`scheduleDeclarativeRetry` 会跳过 held 实例；清掉凭据会改变指纹，之后走 `degradeConnectorForCredential`，不设 held，所以回到 backoff。
- 报错文本和 PR #28037 发布的逐字一致。

- **形态:** one PR, `Fixes #28038`, one file `docs/adr/0097-declarative-connector-instances.md` (+28 −1), `skip-changeset`. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 28161`: GOVERNED, Tier H (1 of 1 path).

Check Changeset is skipped because the synchronize event already carries `skip-changeset`. The dev report shows 21 of 21 derived gate families exit 0.

  - Dev model and effort: `dispatch-gates --tier` gives fable/xhigh for `docs/adr/**`, but this card was developed on opus/medium per the seat's order. Two fable review rounds make up the depth; the review judged that nothing is under-reviewed.

- **范围外去向:** review should-fix 3 is carried by ADR-0143's revoked-grant mechanism. That mechanism has no code yet; when it lands, it owes 0097 a third kind of hold. There is no new card.
- **落地条款:** Tier H. The seat posts the record and this ACCEPT, adds `needs-user-decision`, and requests os-zhuang and hotlong.
